item.title: Designing an LLM Summarization Pipeline: OpenAI API, Ollama, and Local Models
item.description:
Since 2022, I have been bringing LLMs into real product workflows. One part of that work is an internal text summarization and AI application platform that integrates the OpenAI API, Ollama, local models, and batch processing, with the focus on model usage that stays controllable and maintainable.

The details of an internal system like this are not suitable for publication, so this is not a full case study. Instead, it collects the principles and trade-offs I apply when designing and operating a summarization pipeline. API behavior described here was checked against the official documentation at the time of writing (October 2026); check the latest docs before relying on it.

item.title: Proxmox VE and PBS: Planning and Backup Strategy for Small and Mid-sized On-prem Infrastructure
item.description:
Since 2023, I have planned and operated Proxmox VE, Proxmox Backup Server (PBS), GPU servers, and On-prem infrastructure as an operator. The environment runs internal services and AI runtime workloads, and I am responsible for the overall backup strategy.

This is not an installation guide. It summarizes the planning principles I care about in small and mid-sized on-prem environments, plus problems I actually ran into and documented on my blog (the linked posts are written in Traditional Chinese). It does not include hostnames, IP addresses, network layouts, or security details. Configuration advice here is general guidance, and the official Proxmox documentation remains the reference.

item.title: Self-hosted GitLab, Runner, and Harbor: A CI/CD Flow from Source Code to Deployment
item.description:
Since 2022, I have built and maintained self-hosted GitLab, GitLab Runner, Harbor registry, and CI/CD workflows as an Operator, connecting source code, container images, and deployment into one flow.

This is not a setup tutorial. Examples for .gitlab-ci.yml, Runner deployment, and multi-environment deployment are in the GitLab CI/CD Guide: Runner Setup, .gitlab-ci.yml, Harbor, and Deployments, and config.toml options and common variables are in GitLab Runner config.toml Configuration and Common CI/CD Variables. This post covers the other side: why you would run this stack yourself, how the components fit together, and where the time actually goes after a few years. Each problem mentioned below links to the record I wrote at the time on blog.clarence.tw.

item.title: Speech AI and GPU Runtime: Notes on Deploying and Operating Kaldi and Whisper
item.description:
Since 2022, part of my work has been bringing speech recognition technologies such as Kaldi and Whisper, together with GPU runtime, into real systems. That covers model inference, system deployment, and the performance maintenance that follows.

This is not a full case study of a specific project, and it does not include internal architecture, data, or performance numbers. Instead, it describes how I approach this kind of work: how I think about the differences between Kaldi and Whisper, why I stabilize the GPU runtime first, and what I check after deployment. Technical details follow the official documentation, and the troubleshooting lessons come from articles I have published on blog.clarence.tw (written in Chinese).

item.title: How I Work: Backend, AI, DevOps, and Infrastructure
item.description:
I do not treat Backend, AI, DevOps, Infrastructure, and Network as isolated areas. For a product that has to go online, be used, and remain maintainable, these layers eventually become one delivery chain.

Features need stable APIs. Services need reliable CI/CD. Long-running systems need monitoring, backup, network visibility, and security. When a product needs LLMs, Speech AI, or GPU runtime, model integration also has to be deployable, observable, and operable.

item.title: GitLab CI/CD Guide: Runner Setup, .gitlab-ci.yml, Harbor, and Deployments
item.description:
In enterprise DevOps work, I build and maintain GitLab CI/CD workflows that automate everything from code submission to production deployment. This article shares the foundational GitLab CI/CD configuration I rely on.

Reviewed July 11, 2026: The examples now use GitLab Runner authentication tokens, Node.js 24 LTS, and Docker 29.6.1. Version and security defaults continue to change; check the current GitLab Runner registration documentation, Node.js release status, and Docker Engine release notes before production use, then pin images to a version or digest your team has tested.

item.title: High-traffic Web Hosting Operations
item.description:
I have operated a high-traffic hosting environment that hosted more than 4,000 websites. This kind of work is not just about running a web server. It requires capacity planning, monitoring, updates, security, DNS / CDN operations, incident response, and day-to-day maintenance discipline.

At this scale, standardization matters. Every update, certificate change, configuration adjustment, and alert cannot depend only on human memory.
